paths.description: Homepage: primary news discovery, navigation, consent, responsive and preference conditions.
Representative lead NewsArticle: reading, metadata, performance and responsive layout.
Primary signup/form template and input-assistance surface.

findings.summary: The site has no user-preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition probe found no prefers-color-scheme/light-dark CSS, and the dark mobile screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving contrast.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not handled.
findings.evidence: The preference probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules in loaded CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for text, controls, focus indicators, and custom chrome.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent wall obscures all news on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show the Didomi notice covering the complete content area before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, non-obscuring consent surface and preserve a direct equivalent reject action.

findings.summary: Overlays use custom role=dialog containers rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found 2 role=dialog elements but 0 <dialog>, 0 popover, and 0 details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal consent and popover for transient menus, with declarative light dismiss and focus management.

findings.summary: Consent and advertising chrome dominate the initial experience.
findings.evidence: The initial viewport is entirely consent UI; the no-JS browser view then devotes a large early block to advertising before headline content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce consent height and reserve smaller ad slots so editorial content is visible in the first viewport.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport adaptation without container queries.
findings.evidence: Loaded-CSS probe found no @container or container-type usage across homepage, article, and newsletter templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Make reusable cards and navigation components size-aware with container queries and intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Prominent article links are malformed and route through duplicated actu.fr path text.
findings.evidence: Recon found multiple hrefs such as https://actu.fr/https:/actu.fr/normandie/... in the primary homepage feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct URL construction at render time and add link-integrity tests for every feed template.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is slow on both representative templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.81s on home and 4.63s on the article; performance scores were 0.76 and 0.77.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce critical CSS/script contention, and defer consent/ad work until after the main content paints.

findings.summary: A very long main-thread task blocks responsiveness during load.
findings.evidence: Trace summary recorded one 1323.94ms long task and 1273.94ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the task, split work into yieldable chunks, and defer analytics/ad initialization by priority.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and slow dependency chains delay content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 820ms render-blocking savings; HAR confirms a VeryHigh parser stylesheet and slow GTM/consent/script requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer noncritical styles/scripts, and set explicit fetch priorities for the LCP path.

findings.summary: The initial route ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 551 KiB unused JavaScript and 59 KiB unused CSS; HAR transferred 1.06 MB of scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split route features and conditionally load advertising, consent, and account dependencies.

findings.summary: Many linked images produce empty accessible links, and consent link names mismatch visible labels.
findings.evidence: Probe counted 154 empty-text links on home and 57 on article; Lighthouse identified two visible-label/accessibility-name mismatches.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every linked card an accessible name from its headline and ensure aria-label includes the visible consent-link text.

findings.summary: A homepage category label fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1.83:1 for green #2a8749 text over blue #035188, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose a category/background token pair that reaches at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a rendering error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured: <svg> attribute width expected a length but received auto.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the SVG a valid numeric/CSS width and keep the console clean in CI.

findings.summary: Image markup and formats waste bytes and risk layout shift.
findings.evidence: Images audit found 2 missing dimensions, 46 missing srcset, and 51 legacy-format images; Lighthouse also flagged the unsized LCP image.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height, responsive srcset/sizes, and AVIF/WebP sources with appropriate fallbacks.

findings.summary: First-party bundles lack usable source maps and DevTools reports inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps and inspector-issues audits on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish protected production source maps and resolve reported CSP/inspector issues.

findings.summary: Homepage Open Graph metadata has an empty title.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found og:title="" on the homepage, while the article correctly supplies NewsArticle JSON-LD and populated Open Graph fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Populate homepage og:title from the descriptive document title and validate social cards in release checks.

findings.summary: Security policy coverage is incomplete and the consent cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; cookies probe found didomi_token without Secure. CSP, HSTS, and nosniff were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all HTTPS cookies and add explicit least-privilege Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy headers.

findings.summary: Third-party advertising and tracking dominate the initial transfer.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 22 requests and 882,036 bytes to third parties; tracker probe found GTM and DoubleClick, while consent text names 765 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, gate nonessential requests behind consent, batch analytics, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.

findings.summary: Rejecting personalized advertising is not an equivalent one-click choice.
findings.evidence: The wall offers “Tout accepter” directly, while the visible alternative is “Refuser et s’abonner” for €2/month; free rejection requires entering settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent one-click accept and reject controls without coupling rejection to a paid subscription.

findings.summary: Newsletter and location forms lack explicit validation semantics.
findings.evidence: Newsletter probe found the email input has no associated label and is not required; the city search also lacks a label and autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible labels, required/email validation, appropriate autocomplete, and accessible post-interaction error messages.

findings.summary: Most editorial images use legacy formats without responsive candidates.
findings.evidence: Images audit reported 51 legacy images and 46 without srcset among 68 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and right-size each editorial image with srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: Non-browser agents receive a 403 and no structured agent capability is exposed.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetches for home and article returned 403 with zero raw-content coverage; probes found no WebMCP/agent tool registration. JS-disabled Chrome could render SSR content, so this is UA policy rather than a JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit legitimate read-only crawler user agents and expose safe, structured article/search capabilities where appropriate.

taskList.title: Make consent non-blocking and provide equal one-click reject
Cut load-time script and third-party work
Repair malformed feed links and accessible card names
Complete preference, form, metadata and policy hygiene
